digest.component_or_area: check_raw_git_writes.py linting gate and git_adapter seam enforcement
propositions: The existing checker (policy d37e) enforces the mechanism rule (no raw subprocess git) but misses the protocol rule (tracker mutations must go through atomic transactions), allowing out-of-seam compositions like reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 that call git_adapter.add and git_adapter.commit without a lock.

Rule R3 must fire on calls to git-adapter mutation primitives (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) made from outside the sanctioned seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py), detected via import bindings and dynamic-loader bindings.
R3 must not fire inside sanctioned seam files, inside calls marked with durable reasoned # raw-git-ok: comments, or on non-git-adapter method calls like set.add() or session.commit().

Two enumerated out-of-transaction composition sites must carry durable reasoned inline markers: reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (_commit_binding_store_snapshot) and __main__.py:338-351 (_purge_committed_reconciler_locks), both with cites explaining why seam routing is not viable or why the pattern is concurrency-safe.

The module-size gate violation on __main__.py caused by markers must be resolved by extracting the pass-lock lifecycle cluster into _pass_lock_lifecycle.py, preserving patch targets and re-exporting moved callables to __main__ namespace.

R3's first run on the real tree must enumerate zero false positives in src/ and scripts/, confirm the two enumerated sites are the only out-of-transaction compositions, and land with zero unsanctioned violations and zero debt baseline.
